reporting-org.narrative: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

title.narrative: NIHR Global Health: Modelling the effects of integrating diabetic retinopathy services in the Malawi health system

description.narrative:
This research aims to help reduce sight loss from diabetes (DM) in Malawi by developing models to integrate screening and treatment for diabetic retinopathy (DR) within the health system, that can be replicated in other African countries.
Currently, 24 million adults have DM in the African region and this will rise by 134% in the next twenty years. DR is the commonest cause of blindness in working age people. In Africa, 1 in 3 people with DM have DR, and 1 in 6 need urgent treatment to save sight. Unfortunately, health systems in the region offer limited services. In Malawi nearly half a million people with DM require regular eye screening to identify those needing treatment to prevent sight loss. Blindness causes high productivity losses and higher mortality rates.
The integration of eye health in diabetes services is key to controlling blindness in the diabetic population. Screening and treatment programmes for DR are considered “best-buy” cost-effective interventions by WHO. However, they are not yet implemented in the African region, leaving people with DM at risk of blindness. A hindrance to achieving this, despite the existence of cost-effective interventions, are the competing healthcare needs on a healthcare system with severe constraints on resources.
The proposed research intends to use mathematical modelling to consider the integration of DR interventions in the Malawi healthcare system and calculate the health gains generated by such services. This will be used to inform policy makers and health planners when deciding on the interventions prioritized in the national health plans.
This project will be underpinned by an existing healthcare systems model for cardiovascular diseases in Malawi, as part of the Thanzi La Onse (Health for All) modelling project (www.tlomodel.org). We aim to generate data on DR in Malawi to build the model through the following objectives: 1) Identify models for delivery of DR services, analyse cost-effectiveness and appraise applicability to the Malawi health system 2) Estimate the magnitude and factors that predispose people to developing DR 3) Evaluate coherence of national policies for DM and DR service delivery 4) Assess current delivery of DR services in Malawi’s health system 5) Model inclusion of DR services within DM services and the wider health system in Malawi
The project team includes lead researches from the Eye Health Research Group (EHRG) and Health Economics and Policy Unit (HEPU) at KUHeS, the International Centre for Eye Health (ICEH) at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and members of the Diabetes Association and the Ministry of health in Malawi. Their collaboration in the project ensures oversight and integration into previous work and guarantees the coordination required to maximize the success of the project.
The Eye Health Research Group has a long-term partnership with ICEH, as part of a DR-Network of 12 African countries working to strengthen DR services. This will a key route for dissemination of results in the region. The project will be also to the wider scientific community via publications and presentations at international scientific meetings.
Ultimately, we aim to provide policy makers in Malawi with an evidence-based model for integration of DR in health services. The track record of the EHRG and HEPU unit in translating research into policy and working alongside policy makers in Malawi will be instrumental to the project impact
